title: Pauri 35, sound: dharam khandd kaa
tomorrow: Pauri 35, meaning: the realm of knowledge
last: DHARAM KHAND — THE EARTH IS FOR DHARMA.

cards: On a train, a voice comes over the speaker: this stop, Central. Next stop, Riverside. One sentence, two jobs.

It closes the station you're pulling out of and names the one ahead. Nobody has to look out the window to know the trip has moved on. Pauri 35 opens with a sentence built just like that, a hinge between two places.
And as soon as the next place comes into view, one small word starts repeating, as if the speaker keeps turning around and finding more.

teach.b: The hinge: dharam khandd kaa eho dharam, giaan khandd kaa aakhahu karam. First half.
Dharam khandd: the realm of dharma, yesterday's word, sung with a strong double d at the end, khandd. Kaa: of. Eho: this, this very.
Dharam: dharma. So: this is the dharma of the realm of dharma. That's this stop, closing behind us: the earth as a house for right action, each weighed by their deeds.
Second half. Giaan khandd: the realm of knowledge. You met giaan in Pauri 29, wisdom as the meal.
Kaa: of. Aakhahu: tell, speak of it; you can hear aakhan from Pauri 33 in it. Karam: here, the doings, the workings.
So: now tell of the workings of the realm of knowledge. That's the next stop.
The two halves rhyme on their last words: dharam, karam.
Then comes the word that repeats: kete, how many, so many.
Kete pavan paanee vaisantar: so many winds, waters and fires. Kete, kete, kete, line after line, more than a dozen times by the end of the stanza. Tomorrow, what's being counted.

how: Many Sikhs recite Japji Sahib each morning; Pauri 35 opens with a line that closes the realm of dharma and opens the realm of knowledge, then repeats kete, so many, through the rest of the stanza.

games.q: the sound of Pauri 35 — tap the pairs.

s: the first line of Pauri 35 closes one realm and opens the next
this is the way of dharma's realm; now tell of knowledge's realm.
kete means so many, how many.
the two halves of the first line rhyme on dharam and karam
this is the dharma of dharma's realm; now tell the workings of knowledge's realm.

games.q: the announcement says: this stop, the realm of dharma. what does Pauri 35 name next?
games.why: giaan khandd kaa aakhahu karam: now tell of the workings of the realm of knowledge.

practice: Say the first line aloud three times, feeling the first half close and the second half open: dharam khandd kaa eho dharam, giaan khandd kaa aakhahu karam.
Then sit in the pause at a station, doors open, one stop behind you with everything you already know, and something larger ahead. Don't move yet; stay in the pause and breathe.

wordCard.voice: Kete, so many, how many. It opens with a hinge: this is the way of the realm of dharma; now tell of the realm of knowledge, and the word kete begins.

orig.note: Gurmukhi, Japji Pauri 35: this is the dharma of the realm of dharma.

carryVoice: Your line: dharam khandd. One realm closes as the next one opens. That's day two hundred twenty-two.
